title: Composition of quasi-finite ring maps
statement: Let $A\to B$ and $B\to C$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings. Assume that both maps are of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and quasi-finite at every prime of the target in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. Then the composite $A\to C$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime of $C$.

proof.text: Finite type is preserved by composition, by RingHom.FiniteType.comp (Stacks Tag 00F4).

For each base prime p, PrimeSpectrum.preimageHomeomorphFiber identifies the topological fibre of Spec B to Spec A with Spec of the residue fibre ring. Every point q in this fibre is isolated by the hypothesis at q. Transport these open singletons back along the homeomorphism; discreteTopology_iff_isOpen_singleton proves that the topological fibre is discrete. Apply the same argument to Spec C to Spec B.

For a prime p of A, the composite fibre is the inverse image under the continuous map Spec C to Spec B of the discrete fibre over p. Mathlib IsDiscrete.preimage' proves that this inverse image is discrete, since every fibre of Spec C to Spec B is discrete by the preceding step. PrimeSpectrum.comap is functorial, so this is exactly the fibre of the composite. Its singleton at r is open; transport it through PrimeSpectrum.preimageHomeomorphFiber for A to C. Together with finite type from the first step, this proves IsQuasiFiniteAtPrime for every r.
